boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named destinations on distinct, practical downtown corridors and blocks near Hope College, each paired with one verified reason to go.

cards.title: Take the Garden Paths
cards.subtitle: Central Avenue corridor — between 10th and 12th Streets
cards.notes: Enter from Central Avenue and follow the brick walkways past the fountain, gardens, gazebo and seasonal restrooms.
cards.short_summary: A landscaped civic square with paths, public art and a historic fountain.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Holland lists Centennial Park at 250 Central Avenue and identifies gardens, a fountain, pedestrian walkways, a gazebo and other public amenities.
cards.access_notes: City-listed hours are 6:00 a.m.–11:00 p.m. daily; seasonal restrooms are available.

cards.title: Read the City Through Its Objects
cards.subtitle: West 10th Street corridor — at River Avenue
cards.notes: Check current admission and exhibition details, then focus your visit on the Holland history and Dutch art galleries.
cards.short_summary: A downtown museum connecting local settlement history with Dutch art and material culture.
cards.evidence_claim: The museum identifies its location as 31 W. 10th Street and says its galleries cover Holland’s history and feature Dutch artwork from the 1600s through the 1900s.
cards.access_notes: Open on listed museum days; admission normally applies, with free public admission on designated second Mondays.

cards.title: Settle In with Books and Tools
cards.subtitle: South River Avenue corridor — between 12th and 13th Streets
cards.notes: Use the River Avenue entrance for collections, public programs, technology help and reservable Main Library rooms.
cards.short_summary: A full-service public library stop on the south edge of downtown.
cards.evidence_claim: Herrick District Library lists its Main Library at 300 South River and provides public collections, events, technology help and library rooms there.
cards.access_notes: Current posted hours vary by day; some rooms or services may require a library card or reservation.

cards.title: Browse the Market Canopy
cards.subtitle: West 8th Street corridor — at the Eighth Street Marketplace
cards.notes: Check the current market calendar before walking west on 8th Street; browsing is possible without making a purchase.
cards.short_summary: A covered municipal market where the vendor mix changes with the season.
cards.evidence_claim: The official market site places Holland Farmers Market at 150 West 8th Street and documents its permanent canopy and vendor-stall market space.
cards.access_notes: Market operation is schedule-dependent; consult the official calendar before visiting. Dogs are not permitted except service animals.

cards.title: Pair Coffee with Local Music
cards.subtitle: East 9th Street corridor — near College Avenue
cards.notes: Walk one block north from campus, then check the posted music calendar before choosing a drink or snack at the counter.
cards.short_summary: An independent coffeehouse combining a café counter with music programming.
cards.evidence_claim: Lemonjello’s official site describes the business as a coffee and music venue, while Downtown Holland’s dining guide lists it at 61 East 9th Street.
cards.access_notes: Public café access; verify current operating hours and event details on the business site before going.

cards.title: Tour a Mayor’s 1874 Home
cards.subtitle: West 9th Street corridor — west of Pine Avenue
cards.notes: Start at the visitor center and join a scheduled tour to see rooms interpreted around Isaac Cappon and his family.
cards.short_summary: A preserved mayoral residence interpreted to approximately 1900.
cards.evidence_claim: Holland Museum lists Cappon House at 228 W. 9th Street and identifies it as the 1874 home of Holland’s first mayor, restored in part to its circa-1900 appearance.
cards.access_notes: Seasonal guided tours begin at the Cappon House Visitor Center; off-season visits require advance arrangements.

cards.title: Compare a Working-Family Home
cards.subtitle: West 9th Street corridor — near Washington Avenue
cards.notes: Visit on the paired historic-house tour and compare this compact 1871 interpretation with the nearby Cappon House.
cards.short_summary: A small surviving home interpreted through Holland’s working-class history.
cards.evidence_claim: Holland Museum lists Settlers House at 190 W. 9th Street and says the circa-1867 building survived the 1871 fire and is restored to an 1871 appearance.
cards.access_notes: Seasonal tours start at the nearby Cappon House Visitor Center; appointments are required outside the stated season.

cards.title: See the National Guard Exhibit
cards.subtitle: West 9th Street corridor — just west of River Avenue
cards.notes: Call the Holland Museum before going; the Armory’s National Guard exhibition is free but available by appointment.
cards.short_summary: A former civic and military building with a focused local National Guard display.
cards.evidence_claim: Holland Museum places The Holland Armory at 16 W. 9th Street and states that its 1921–1998 National Guard exhibition is free to visit by appointment.
cards.access_notes: The exhibition is free but appointment-only; call the Holland Museum at the number on the official page to arrange access.

cards.title: Locate the Civic Centerpiece
cards.subtitle: South River Avenue corridor — opposite Centennial Park
cards.notes: Use the River Avenue façade as a visual anchor, then cross toward Centennial Park for a closer look at the civic core.
cards.short_summary: A named municipal landmark anchoring the River Avenue civic block.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Holland’s official facilities directory lists City Hall at 270 S River Avenue.
cards.access_notes: Exterior viewing is public; interior access is limited to municipal business hours and public meetings or services.

cards.title: Find the 1941 Caboose
cards.subtitle: Lincoln Avenue corridor — at the Padnos Transportation Center
cards.notes: Continue north on Lincoln Avenue to photograph the restored rail car beside the active transportation center.
cards.short_summary: A museum-operated railroad artifact displayed beside Holland’s passenger station.
cards.evidence_claim: Holland Museum identifies Pere Marquette Caboose No. A967 as a 1941 rail car located at the Padnos Transportation Center, 171 Lincoln Avenue.
cards.access_notes: The exterior display is at an active transportation center; remain in public pedestrian areas and do not enter rail operating space.
